title: José Martí's birth chart
metaDescription: José Martí's chart, computed from a sourced birth date: Sun at 8.8° Aquarius. Birth time unknown, so no houses or rising sign.
lede: The chart's headline is a conjunction: the Sun and Mars within 0.5°, identity wired to drive. Two bodies in the same degree are not read as neighbours but as a merger: whatever one wants, the other is already funding.

blocks.title: Where the Sun actually stood
blocks.text: The Sun sits at 8.8° Aquarius — the first decan, 0°–10°, which the tradition sub-rules by Saturn. Degrees matter more than the sign label here: two people born a fortnight apart share Aquarius and share almost nothing else about where the Sun actually stood.

blocks.title: Closer to the ground
blocks.text: Closer in, Mercury stands at 20.1° Capricorn; Venus stands at 12.6° Capricorn; Mars stands at 8.3° Aquarius. The tradition reads a mind that trusts the measured and the checked from Mercury, taste for the substantial and the lasting from Venus, drive that argues its way forward from Mars.

blocks.title: The angles that hold
blocks.text: The Sun and Mars hold the closest angle here — a conjunction, 0.5° wide. A conjunction concentrates rather than balances — the pair burns one fuel line. Behind it, Saturn sextile Neptune at 1.3°, and Venus trine Saturn at 1.4° — both still well inside the orbs this site uses. These are the day-proof angles — present at midnight, present at noon, present at the next midnight.

blocks.title: The standing structure
blocks.text: The Moon stands apart from every major angle the day held — the tradition reads an unaspected planet as a voice that speaks on its own schedule, unmodulated by the rest of the chart.

blocks.title: The classical map
blocks.text: Two planets here sit in a sign the classical scheme scores. The Sun in Aquarius at 8.8° is in detriment — the planet opposite its home, working against the grain; Jupiter in Sagittarius at 17.3° is in domicile — the planet in its own sign, running on home rules. The old table grades terrain, not talent — a placement in fall works uphill, nothing more.

blocks.title: The shape of the whole
blocks.text: Among the 10 placements whose signs hold for the whole day, the elements divide 5 earth, 2 air, 2 fire, 1 water; by modality, 4 fixed, 3 mutable, 3 cardinal. An earth emphasis reads as patience with material reality — slow hands, durable results. Not one planet was retrograde, so the whole chart reads in direct motion.

blocks.title: The Moon, and how far it can move
blocks.text: The Moon stayed in Virgo for the whole of that day at the birthplace, covering 13.9° between midnight and midnight. Whatever the unrecorded hour was, it happened inside one Moon sign — the degree floats, the sign holds. At the noon reference it stands at 22.8°.
